data.title: Court reinstates $7B 'Solar for All' program axed by Trump
data.description:
A federal court has rebuffed the Trump administration’s effort to slash a $7 billion program that seeks to provide rooftop solar power in disadvantaged communities. 

Judge Mary McElroy, a Trump appointee in Rhode Island, vacated the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) move to terminate the Solar For All (SFA) program and claw back the funding.

The program in question was funded by the Biden administration’s Inflation Reduction Act. The Trump-era One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) rescinded any “unobligated” balances in the program.

McElroy said that under these laws, the EPA did not have the power to rescind funds that were already awarded.

“The OBBBA did not convert SFA funding into a lump-sum amount subject to EPA’s discretion. Instead, Congress’s clear intent was that EPA continue to administer the already obligated SFA grants. Defendants acted contrary to this intent, and with no other statutory authority, when they terminated the SFA program,” she wrote. 

The judge therefore declared the program’s termination unlawful and tossed out the EPA’s move to do so.

Her decision represents a blow to the Trump administration’s efforts to reduce government spending and target Biden-era climate programs.

An EPA spokesperson said in an email that it is “reviewing the decision and considering options for appeal.”

Environmental advocates, including those who sued over the decision, lauded the judge’s ruling.

“The court ruled the Trump Administration never should have terminated Solar for All because Congress intended it to continue, and EPA broke the law when it killed the program and pocketed the money,” said Southern Environmental Law Center senior attorney Nick Torrey in a written statement  “Electricity bills are skyrocketing, so low-cost solar projects — which guarantee big savings — are needed now more than ever. Today’s victory means EPA must stop sitting on the $7 billion in funding for this program and start getting it out into communities to provide hardworking American families much-needed relief.”

data.title: Live updates: Trump defends White House ban of 3 media outlets, announces Medicaid drug price deal
data.description:
President Trump said Friday he was kicking CNN, MS NOW and Politico out of the White House, “effective immediately,” claiming “their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS!” as the reason. He suggested more outlets would be banned in the future.

The news came just ahead of Trump holding an announcement about Medicaid drug prices Friday afternoon.

Vice President Vance visited Iowa for a rally on Friday. He was joined by Republican gubernatorial candidate Zach Lahn, who is running against Democratic state Auditor Rob Sand. Vance laid into Sand for more than five minutes at the rally.

The rally’s location is the turf of Democratic Senate candidate Josh Turek, who is campaigning against Rep. Ashley Hinson (R-Iowa) for the open seat. Hinson reportedly won’t attend the Vance event.

The Pentagon told congressional leaders this week that the cost of the Iran war through Sept. 3 had exceeded $43 billion, not including damage estimates to sites hit.

data.title: GOP Senators defend Federal Reserve's decision
data.description:
Welcome to The Hill’s Business & Economy newsletter

The Big Story 

GOP senators rebuff Trump attacks on Federal Reserve

President Trump’s sharp criticisms of the Federal Reserve’s decision to raise interest rates are making some Republicans uncomfortable.

© Alex Brandon, Associated Press

Trump declared that “Interest Rates in the United States should be 1%, or less, because we are the Best Credit in the World — BY FAR,” calling on the central bank to “LOWER THE INTEREST RATES … AND FAST!”

 

He later told reporters that he’s “relying” on Kevin Warsh, the Fed chair, to cut rates.

 

But the president gave him the greenlight to “vote with the board” since they had majority support for raising interest rates to between 3.75 percent and 4 percent.

 

Trump lambasted the other board members as “very hostile” and “very political.”

 

But Republican senators said the Fed members only followed their mandate to keep inflation in check.

 

“I have no problem with the Fed decision. I think the Fed exercised their independence, which is what we elect them to do, and I think the markets have responded accordingly,” Sen. Mike Rounds (R-S.D.) said, calling the financial markets “a true barometer of what’s going on.”

 

Stocks fell immediately after the Fed announced the rate hike but then surged on Thursday, with the S&P 500 Index and the Nasdaq rising 1.14 percent and 1.69 percent, respectively.

 

“That’s going to help the president long-term,” Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.) said.

 

“It may not be what he wants short-term but to have a Fed in which the market has confidence in their ability to look at the economy as a whole, that’s a very important thing for the president to have on his side long-term,” he continued. “The Fed did what they were supposed to do.”

 

Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) also defended the Fed’s action.

 

“They’re trying their best to ensure that they’re meeting their mission of keeping inflation at the rate that’s called for in their charter,” he said. “It’s always a bit of a judgment call but that’s the conclusion they came to.”

 

Though Thune acknowledged the rate hike “is not going to be helpful in terms of lowering costs in the near term.”

data.title: Shaheen blocks $2.8 billion weapons sale to Israel, joining House counterpart
data.description:
The top Democrat on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee has exercised a hold on a $2.8 billion weapons sale to Israel, The Hill has learned, allying with her counterpart in the House and underscoring deep mistrust with the Trump administration and Israeli government. 

Sen. Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.) has expressed frustration that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has done nothing to address concerns from, specifically, Democratic lawmakers over the high civilian death tolls in Gaza, Israel’s bombing in Syria and escalating violence against Palestinians by extremist Israeli settlers in the West Bank. 

The weapons package includes 40,000 one-ton bombs, munitions that the former Biden administration held back from sending to Israel for its indiscriminate destruction, contributing to the high-death toll in the Gaza Strip.

An estimated 70,000 Palestinians were killed over the course of the three-year war between Israel and Hamas, according to Palestinian health officials, but that does not distinguish between militants and civilians. 

Shaheen, as the top Democrat on the Senate Foreign Relations panel, has authority to hold back the Trump administration from moving ahead on weapons sales over a certain dollar amount. It’s generally an informal consultative process, where the State Department works to address a lawmaker’s concerns and get the green light before moving ahead on the arms sale. 

Semafor first reported that Shaheen is exercising the hold, and that she put it in place in July. Rep. Gregory Meeks (D-N.Y.), her counterpart on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, made the rare decision Wednesday to publicly announce he placed a hold on the military sale. 

Meeks said he had concerns over whether Netanyahu’s government would use American-provided weapons in accordance with international humanitarian law and U.S. law. 

CNN asked Shaheen Wednesday for her reaction to Meeks’s hold, saying, “all of us share concern about what Israel is doing.” 

“What they’re doing in Gaza, they’re bombing in places like Syria and what that means for any peaceful solution in the Middle East,” she said.

“Netanyahu needs to hear from America that we don’t like what he’s doing. We don’t like what’s happening in the West Bank where settler violence is killing Palestinians, sending them out of their homes, disrupting basic infrastructure. And the Netanyahu administration has basically done nothing to address that,” Shaheen continued.

data.title: Mullin responds to Salazar's ad attacking Trump's immigration crackdown
data.description:
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin on Friday defended the Trump administration’s immigration policy after a Republican lawmaker endorsed by President Trump said ICE has “gone too far” by arresting people without criminal records.

Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar (R-Fla.), made a notable break from Trump in a new campaign ad for her reelection bid in Florida.

“Mr. President, some of your immigration enforcement efforts have gone too far,” he said in the ad, which will run on TV and online in South Florida.

“In July, 50% of the 50,000 people that were detained had no criminal record,” she added. “The same Hispanics who helped you get to the White House in 2024 feel betrayed today.”

CNN’s Dana Bush pressed the Homeland Security chief on Salazar’s comments, noting that Salazar currently represents a majority-Hispanic district.

“We don’t pick and choose which laws we enforce. We enforce the immigration policy that Congress passed and obligated Department of Homeland Security to enforce,” Mullin said.

He also asserted that DHS was not basing its arrests on quotas set by the White House, and that there has “never” been a conversation with the White House about such a target.

Mullin said ICE prioritizes people with serious criminal histories but will also arrest other people who are in the country illegally when agents encounter them during enforcement operations.

Bash noted that Salazaar was citing DHS data obtained through a Freedom of Information Act request showing that half of the roughly 50,000 people detained in July had no criminal record — a distinction which Mullin rejected.

“I will say that’s actually not true,” he said, arguing that the people who entered the country illegally were already criminals since they broke the law.

“When you broke the law and you came into this country illegally, you chose to become a criminal at that point, regardless,” he said.

data.title: Republican misgenders McBride at candidate forum before removal
data.description:
Republican nominee Joe Arminio was removed from a forum debate in Wilmington, Delaware after misgendering his opponent, Rep. Sarah McBride (D-Del.).

During the debate between the candidates competing for Delaware’s lone congressional district, Arminio used the incorrect pronouns when referring to McBride – who made history in 2024 as the first openly transgender member of Congress.

“I’m sorry to have to say that the representative from Delaware, through the net of his comments and his actions, on balance has contributed,” Arminio said before being interrupted by the crowd. “I would like to show respect to the speaker, that would be nice.”

When he finished his opening remarks, moderator Ken Grant warned Arminio that this was his final warning, saying “if you fail to show respect to anyone else on this stage, you’ll be asked to leave.”

Arminio admitted he “committed an error before” and he does “acknowledge it.”

“It’s not the first error I’ve made in this campaign, or at any point in my future life,” he added.

When discussing healthcare in the forum later on, Arminio pointed to Sen. Chris Coons (D-Del.) and McBride – blaming rising costs on the “gentlemen like the two up here with me in the Democratic Party.”

He was interrupted again by the crowd before being asked to leave the stage – though McBride attempted to intervene.

“I want to say here, I don’t want this gentleman to not have the ability to–,” she said, before being cut off by the moderator.

Arminio was still told to leave by the moderator and event organizers.

McBride’s office deferred to the lawmaker’s statement on social media posted Friday, stating, “I am always so proud to represent Delaware and Delawareans.”

“Nothing – and certainly not politicians seeking to go viral – will ever distract me from my laser focus on lowering the cost of gas, groceries, housing, childcare, and healthcare,” she continued.

Arminio’s misgendering of McBride is not the first time the first-term lawmaker has faced jabs from her Republican colleagues over her identity. In 2025, a House Foreign Affairs subcommittee hearing ended abruptly when Rep. Keith Self (R-Texas) referred to McBride as “mister.”

Rep. Mary Miller (R-Ill.) in the same year also introduced McBride as “the gentleman from Delaware” ahead of her first floor speech as a newly elected lawmaker.

Arminio’s campaign did not respond to The Hill’s request for immediate comment.

data.title: Nearly 30 years later, Princess Diana's 'revenge dress' goes up for auction
data.description:
(NewsNation) — Princess Diana’s iconic “revenge dress” is going up for auction — nearly three decades after she made headlines wearing it.

The striking black dress, worn by Diana on the night her then-husband, King Charles III, publicly acknowledged his infidelity, is being offered by Sotheby’s with a presale estimate of $150,000 to $300,000.

The dress went on public display Friday in London as it begins an international tour ahead of its December auction in New York.

Diana wore the figure-hugging, off-the-shoulder silk dress by Greek designer Christina Stambolian to a gala at London’s Serpentine Gallery on June 29, 1994 — the same day a television interview aired in which Charles acknowledged his affair.

Morgane Halimi, Sotheby’s global head of handbags and fashion, said Diana used fashion to express herself and reclaim control of her own story.

Images of her wearing the dress, paired with a sapphire necklace, black pumps and bright red nail polish, quickly spread around the world. The following day, The Sun famously declared: “Revenge is chic.”

The dress became one of the most recognizable looks associated with Diana, known for her fashion influence and was among the world’s most photographed women.

The “people’s princess” later acknowledged the affair during a 1995 interview, famously saying, “There were three of us in this marriage,” referring to Charles’s relationship with Camilla Parker-Bowles, now Queen Camilla.

Charles and Diana divorced in 1996. The Princess of Wales was killed in a Paris car crash the following year at age 36.

The dress is being auctioned for the first time since 1997, when Diana sold it along with other clothing to raise money for AIDS charities.

Sotheby’s expects the dress could sell for significantly more than its presale estimate. In 2023, a red sweater featuring a sheep design that Diana wore to a polo match sold for $1.1 million, setting a record for an item owned by the late princess.

The “revenge dress” will remain on display in London through Sept. 24 before traveling to Hong Kong and Geneva. It will then be offered at auction in New York on Dec. 9.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

data.title: Spanberger announces tightened data center restrictions, clean energy mandates in Virginia
data.description:
Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger (D) on Friday announced a new proposal to tighten restrictions on data center developments in the state. 

The governor’s “Data Center Accountability Framework” outlines several objectives for the commonwealth’s approach to these projects, including cutting down on noise pollution and water use tied to these projects and promoting clean energy and boosting local jobs. 

Spanberger signed an executive order establishing a “rapid-response” AI task force and directing the commonwealth’s chief energy officer to publish a toolkit to help local communities navigate proposed data center projects. 

Additionally, Spanberger’s directive bans state agencies and employees from entering into nondisclosure agreements that keep any information about these planned developments secret. 

The governor expressed her commitment to work with Virginia’s General Assembly to pass legislation aligned with the rest of this framework’s goals.

“The legislature has done so much to raise this issue in the last few months, and I look forward to working with them to codify parts of this plan into Virginia law,” Spanberger said in a Friday statement. 

“At the end of the day, we all want the same thing: we want Virginia to be a national leader in data center accountability,” the moderate Democratic official continued. 

The new Virginia framework follows recent pushes from other governors to place restrictions on data centers in their states. 

Nevada Gov. Joe Lombardo (R) also signed an executive order on Friday that seeks to stop data center costs from being passed on to local communities as he faces a tight reelection contest against state Attorney General Aaron Ford (D). 

On Thursday, Maryland Gov. Wes Moore (D) said he would “absolutely sign” a moratorium on new data center construction projects in his state. Deb Haaland, the Democratic candidate in New Mexico’s gubernatorial race, also supported a similar push this week. 

Texas Gov. Greg Abbott (R), who is running for reelection, directed the state’s water development board this week to penalize new data centers that fail to meet water use requirements. 

“Data centers must share the duty to protect Texas water,” the incumbent governor said in a statement announcing this directive. 

Northern Virginia has seen a surge in new data center construction projects, with the region being dubbed “Data Center Alley” because of the sheer number of centers in the area.

Nicole Riley, the director of Virginia governmental affairs for the Data Center Coalition, a trade association representing industry members, expressed the group’s commitment to working with state lawmakers “to ensure workable, balanced policies” in a Friday statement following Spanberger’s announcement. 

“If done right, there is a path for continued job creation, responsible investment, and clean energy deployment that protects ratepayers and delivers benefits for families and communities,” Riley said. 

“However, significant and abrupt policy changes without meaningful stakeholder engagement could prove unworkable and jeopardize the real tangible benefits this industry can create,” the director continued. “We hope the implementation of this process will be based in fact and evidence, and account for the tens of thousands of jobs and billions of dollars of economic activity connected to digital infrastructure.”

data.title: Trump says CNN, MS NOW, Politico banned from White House
data.description:
President Trump on Friday said he was banning CNN, MSNOW and Politico from the White House, a move sure to draw fierce pushback from D.C.’s press corps.

Trump said in a Truth Social post that the ban would be “effective immediately” for those outlets, “as a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS!” He suggested more outlets would be banned in the future.

He called CNN “fake news,” and targeted MSNOW, saying the outlet changed its name over “lack of viewership and credibility.”

He also railed against the $8 million the government pays for Politico Pro subscriptions, calling it “illegal and ridiculous.”

“An All Time Record, directly from the United States Government, under Crooked Joe Biden, in order to keep them ‘alive,’ Seems like corruption to me!),” he wrote.

The Hill reached out to all three outlets for comment.

“Media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America,” he continued. “Other Fake News Media Outlets to follow.”

Trump has tried to ban outlets from White House coverage before. Last year, he barred The Associated Press and excluded The Wall Street Journal from traveling in the press pool.

DEVELOPING …
